newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Croda bullish on acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Croda bullish on acquisition.

text.p: British speciality chemicals maker Croda International Plc strengthened its presence in the personal care chemicals industry by acquiring STOA S.A. Group of France, a specialist in skin care chemicals, the company said on Wednesday.

The British group said it was paying 40 million pounds cash and absorbing a net debt of nine million stg in a transaction which was expected to enhance its earnings from the current financial year itself.
Croda also said its profits for the first half would be in line with that of last year, despite the strength of the sterling which continued to pinch on its profitability.
The company's optimistic forecast combined with the acquisition pushed up its share price by 36 pence to 307 1/2p at 1000 GMT.
Croda's group finance director Barbara Richmond, however, told Reuters the company's profits for the whole year were likely to be hit by more than eight million stg.
Richmond said Croda's STOA acquisition would increase the share of its oleochemicals to a "significant proportion" of its turnover which was close to 500 million stg in 1996.
She said the group would retain all of its about 60 staff and expand its business into America and then outside France in Europe.
Currently, a bulk of Sederma's business, about 65 percent is concentrated in France, riding on the back of the country's strong cosmetic industry.
STOA reported post-tax profits of 3.5 million stg in 1996 and had net assets of 3.4 million excluding debt.
